# KuroKit MCP

KuroKit watches web pages, RSS feeds, and official APIs. It tells an AI assistant when something changes.

Official setup guide: https://kurokit.com/docs/mcp
Dashboard: https://kurokit.com
Pricing: https://kurokit.com/pricing
Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/kurokit-webpage-change-mo/fndfgkdjhbaoiadepfhgmhbgfjgfpiao
Edge extension: https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/kurokit-webpage-change-/oiohkchggekefhcdamceinpmabpfiifk

## Endpoint

- MCP URL: https://mcp.kurokit.com/mcp
- Transport: Streamable HTTP
- Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

If the client lists KuroKit in its own connector or MCP marketplace, use that listing and complete OAuth. Use a manually pasted Bearer token only for a custom remote server.

Token page: https://kurokit.com/dashboard/mcp

Do not tell the user to open https://kurokit.com/oauth/authorize. It only works when the MCP client opens it with ?client_id= in the address bar.

## First run

1. Create a KuroKit account.
2. For webpage watches, install the browser extension (Chrome or Edge) and allow the watched site.
3. Add the MCP URL to the AI app, or use the app's KuroKit listing.
4. Call listMonitors to check the connection.
5. Create a monitor for the user's page, RSS feed, or official API.

RSS and official-API watches do not need the extension. Webpage watches need the extension because MCP cannot use the user's browser session.

## Client notes

- Claude: docs/connect-claude.md
- Cursor: docs/connect-cursor.md
- ChatGPT/Codex: docs/connect-chatgpt.md
- Grok/Grok Bot: docs/connect-grok-bot.md
- Another client: docs/connect-any-client.md
- Support matrix: docs/client-support.md

Grok and Grok Bot accept a custom remote MCP server. Meta Muse supports MCP through its Connector Platform, but KuroKit is not a reviewed Muse connector. OpenAI dots uses plugins, and KuroKit is not a published plugin. Do not claim KuroKit is listed in the Muse or dots directories, and do not tell users that a direct custom MCP URL works in dots.

## Workflow automation (push)

For n8n, Make, Zapier, or your own service, use a webhook. Add `webhook` to notifyChannels and pass webhookUrl; KuroKit POSTs signed JSON (`schema_version: 2`), timeout 5s, retries 1m/5m/30m/30m (5 attempts total). `getEvents` is pull-only; there is no MCP match stream. Guide: docs/webhooks.md.

## Common errors

- No tools or 401: create a new token, paste it into the app's settings, reload.
- "Not in the MCP catalog": choose Add custom / manual remote server, use https://mcp.kurokit.com/mcp in lowercase.
- Last check blank: open the watched page, click the extension, and make sure This site says Allowed.
- First check has 0 events: normal; it saves a snapshot. Wait for the second check.
- n8n/Make/Zapier receives nothing: check Webhook, use the production HTTPS URL, activate the workflow, and return 2xx within 5s. See docs/webhooks.md.

## Plans

The free plan includes one active monitor and does not expire. Current prices and limits come from https://kurokit.com/pricing. Do not invent plan numbers.
